blocks.text: Each browser token validator uses a JSON Web Token (JWT) that is issued by your identity provider (IdP) to enforce authentication requirements.
Your IdP's JWT must contain the following token claims when configuring a browser token validator:

blocks.item: Subject (sub): Identifies the principal that is the subject of the JWT. This claim represents the user or entity making the request.
Audience (aud): Specifies the intended recipients of the JWT.
Issuer (iss): Identifies the issuer of the JWT.

blocks.text: You can use jwt.io to inspect and extract the required preceding information from a JWT issued by your application's IdP.
On the Browser Token Validator page (Authentication > User Authentication > Browser Token Validator), you can:

blocks.item: Add a Browser Token Validator
On the Browser Token Validator page, click Add.
The Add Browser Token Validator drawer appears.
In the Add Browser Token Validator drawer:
Name: Enter the name of the browser token validator.
Application Segments: Select the name of the application segment with Browser Access enabled.
Under Claim Requirements, click Add Claim to enter the following information from the JWT issued by your application's IdP:
aud: Add the value listed from the JWT's aud.
iss: Add the value listed from the JWT's iss.
sub: Add the value listed from the JWT's sub.
Depending on your application's IdP, the values might differ from aud, iss, or sub.
Select a Validation Type and depending on your selection:
Client JWKs URL: Enter your JSON Web Key's (JWK's) URL from your application's IdP.
Certificates and Public Keys: Upload the certificate used by your application's IdP to sign JWTs.
See image.
Click Save.
Edit a Browser Token Validator
On the Browser Token Validator page and under Actions, click the Edit icon for the browser token validator.
The Update Browser Token Validator drawer appears.
In the Update Browser Token Validator drawer:
Name: Edit the name of the token validator.
Application Segments: Select the name of the application segment with Browser Access enabled.
Under Claim Requirements, you can edit any of the claim requirements and their values or click Add Claim to create more claim requirements.
Depending on your selection as a Validation Type:
Client JWKs URL: Edit the JSON Web Key's (JWK's) URL.
Certificates and Public Keys: Upload a new certificate or public key used by your application's IdP to sign JWTs.
See image.
Click Save.
Delete a Browser Token Validator
On the Browser Token Validator page and under Actions, click the Delete icon for the browser token validator.
The Confirm: Delete Action window appears.
See image.
Click Delete to confirm deletion of the browser token validator.

blocks.heading: Public Key Format of a Browser Token Validator

blocks.text: After you have added the browser token validator and if you want to configure it to verify JWTs, you can opt to supply the public key in PEM format.
The general guidelines for the public key in PEM format are:

blocks.item: Contains the standard BEGIN and END PUBLIC KEY PEM headers
Follows the standard Rivest–Shamir–Adleman (RSA) algorithm for a PEM format

openssl pkey -in public.pem -pubin -text -noout
